subject: Post-call: Skyline latency & throughput qualification
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@skyline.ai>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Skyline latency & throughput qualification

Hi Samira / Miguel — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have alignment on the A/B work you asked for.

Call highlights (short):
- Priority metrics: p95 and p99 latency at realistic sequence lengths, sustained tokens/sec for 95th percentile traffic, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Current baseline you mentioned: HyperscalerX managed endpoint (512-token average) showed ~p95 220ms, p99 ~480ms, ~18 tokens/sec steady-state (your in-house numbers).
- Key constraints: cold vs warm KV-cache behavior, burst patterns, and request routing (regional failover).

Proposed Redwood qualification matrix (48–72h pilot):
1) Workloads: seq_len {128, 512, 2048}, prompt mix (short/medium/long) from your sample corpus.
2) Modes: Redwood Hosted (default), Redwood Dedicated reserve (N=1 GPU config), and HyperscalerX managed endpoint as control.
3) Vars: batch sizes {1,8,32}, cache warm/cold, model quantization profiles (fp16 vs 4-bit).
4) Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99, tail stalls (ms), tokens/sec sustained, cost per 1k tokens (including infra).

Concrete asks:
- Samira: please upload the sample prompt set and representative traffic distribution (peak qps windows) — that will make the A/B apples-to-apples.
- Miguel: confirm whether we should include your LLM routing layer in the loop or test direct endpoint only.
- Internal: Grace, can you run an initial smoke sweep (128 + 512, batch=1/8) and drop results to Drive? Karthik, can you prepare the public-hyperscaler config we should emulate so the control run matches their flags.

Attachments: I started a short test harness and included an initial smoke CSV (attached) and a short config diff we expect to try.

Next steps / timeline:
- Smoke sweep (internal) -> 24h
- Full A/B run with Skyline corpus -> 48–72h after smoke
- Recap + decision call -> 2 business days after full run

If that timeline works, I’ll lock in owners and share the HubSpot mutual action plan.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Evelyn — thanks, this looks great and comprehensive. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority is p99 and sustained tokens/sec. If you can show a defensible p99 improvement at 512/2048 sequences without blowing up cost, that’s the key business case for us.
- We will upload a 1k prompt sample set (mix of short/medium/long) by EOD PST. Please treat it as sensitive — we’ll share via the Drive link you provide.
- On routing: for the first pass, please test direct endpoint only. We’ll add our routing layer in follow-ups.

On timeline — 48–72h for the full run is preferred. Also, quick question on egress: do you have a standard statement for regional egress (we need to confirm with our security team)?

Thanks — Samira

Subject: Re: Post-call: Skyline latency & throughput qualification

Thanks — ran the smoke sweep this morning and dropped a quick CSV (latency_results_v1.csv) to the shared Drive. Short summary from the smoke:

- Redwood Hosted (N=2 shard): seq_len=512, batch=1 -> p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms, tokens/sec ~22 (warm cache).
- Dedicated reserve (single GPU, 4-bit quant) seq_len=512, batch=8 -> p95 ~160ms, p99 ~390ms, tokens/sec burst ~45 then equilibrates to ~28 tokens/sec.
- Cold cache conditions raised p99 by ~1.6x across runs, so cache-warm behavior is critical for tail numbers.

Test matrix I used (short):
- seq_len: 128/512/2048
- batch: 1/8/32
- cache: cold (first pass)/warm (after 5k tokens)
- quant: fp16 / 4-bit int (QK-based)

Action items assigned: 
- Grace: run full Dedicated matrix (estimated 24h) and export raw trace + token throughput curves.
- Karthik: spin up the HyperscalerX config (flags and runtime knobs) and provide the run script so the control is reproducible.
- Evelyn: coordinate Drive upload from Samira and confirm security egress note for the external team.

I attached the smoke CSV and a short config diff that highlights kernels/flags we toggled. Notably, we saw better tail behavior with continuous batching heuristics and an aggressive KV prefetch on Dedicated.

Grace O'Connor
Perf & Bench Engineer, Redwood Inference
